$comment: Registry of 4K clip sources. Every entry was probed live on 2026-08-12; 'verified' records what was actually measured, not what the site claims. Win4K.Core.Catalogs.CatalogRefresher (C#; scripts/harvest.py retired 2026-10-13) refreshes the entries marked harvest:auto into catalog-<id>.json: Apple manifest schema, so Win4K.Core.Apple.AppleManifest parses them unchanged, plus schema-v2 extension fields. The copies here are the embedded fallback; in-app refreshes write to %LOCALAPPDATA%/Win4KScreensavers/catalogs.

verified.note: Professional RED-shot stock footage, 22-70s per clip. Aspect is mostly DCI 1.90:1, so a 16:9 display crops slightly — panscan handles it. The 2.37:1 items are letterboxed and worth excluding.
verified.reharvest: 2026-10-13: 1316 files (upstream grew; harvest.py and the C# port agreed exactly). 47 are byte-identical re-uploads in '_YYYYMM' mirror items (Water614KRes_201507, ThinSmoke974KRes_201507, one _201511) and are dropped by (file name, size), leaving 1269.

groups.name: scenic
groups.note: 18 items are landscape/nature/aerial; 12 are element shots (smoke, fire, particles, clock) which make good abstract screensavers but are not scenery.

groups.name: pixabay-mirror
groups.note: 183 items mirrored from Pixabay; 54 files are >=4K including one 7680x4320. Key-free path to Pixabay content.

verified.reharvest: 2026-10-13: 19 >=4K of 125 search hits. harvest.py's 9 was an undercount: urllib rejects the collection URLs of ids containing spaces ('NISAR Mission Video') and it skipped them silently. The C# harvester escapes them and reads dimensions from each asset's metadata.json (ExifTool dump) instead of ffprobing.
verified.note: Low yield relative to its size — the library is overwhelmingly 1080p, and filenames carry no resolution marker, so each candidate has to be measured. 9 of 98 candidates measured >=4K in the first harvest. Worth it for one standout: 'Earth from Space in 4K, Expedition 65 Edition', 4096x2160, 3000s at 10.8 Mbps, which alone cuts into dozens of orbital clips.
Schema-identical to Apple's own manifest. Mirrored as files rather than fetched — there is no queryable upstream. Refresh by re-pulling from the AerialVideos repo.

feeds.note: 25 more assets than resources-16.tar, plus 59 subcategories and a 687-entry caption file.
Carries a real timeOfDay field on every asset, which Apple's modern manifest does not.
Cheapest bytes-per-second in the whole survey — 0.40 MB/s of playback.

verified.method: Extracted a 2160p frame from mid-video with yt-dlp and inspected it. 3 of 8 channels tested were clean; the other 5 burn in persistent branding.
verified.note: Never add a channel here without running the frame check — branding is invisible in search results and thumbnails. Cut with stream copy (no --force-keyframes-at-cuts): 13 s vs 3 min for the same 20 s 4K cut.

channels.note: Purpose-built screensaver channel: '(No Sound)' 4K uploads running 1-12 hours each. Best single YouTube source found. Mixes real aerial footage with abstract/AI-generated loops — both useful, but check which you are cutting.

picks.title: Grand Canyon from Above (No Sound) — 1 Hour

channels.note: Cinematic FPV. Clean, but fast motion with visible motion blur — less restful than slow drone work, and compresses harder.

picks.title: One Hour Cinematic FPV Drone Film

channels.note: Clean aerial, though the subject matter is narrow (golf courses, UK countryside).

rejected.reason: burned-in name, URL and IG handle, lower-left

verified.note: Unauthenticated calls return 401. Keys are free and instant. Pexels exposes per-rendition width/height, which makes it the only one that can be filtered to the display resolution reliably — directly relevant to the resolution-matching rework.

rejected.reason: All 159 download links are dead. The site is up and its metadata is accurate (vendor demos at 3840x2160, some >100 Mbps), but every file is hosted on Google Drive and every one returns 404 'does not exist'. Verified against a control: a live-but-restricted Drive file returns 401, not 404.
8 of 120 sampled videos are >=3840 wide, and most of those are diagrams, charts or demos rather than scenery. One usable item (Iceland volcano eruption, 3840x2160).
download.blender.org returns 403 to scripted requests, and the films are narrative animation — wrong texture for ambient wallpaper regardless.
Google TV / Chromecast archives are stills capped near 2560px, not video. Samsung and LG have no public manifest and no community mapping to build on.
libmpv plays .m3u8 natively so support is nearly free, but nature cams are overwhelmingly 1080p and a stream cannot be cached, which defeats the offline design.
